questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: The value of \(\cot x+\cot(60^\circ+x)+\cot(120^\circ+x)\) is equal to:
questions.explanation:
Pair the last two terms with \(\cot A+\cot B=\dfrac{\sin(A+B)}{\sin A\sin B}\). Since \(\sin(120^\circ+x)=\sin(60^\circ-x)\):

\[\cot(60^\circ+x)+\cot(120^\circ+x)=\frac{\sin(180^\circ+2x)}{\sin(60^\circ+x)\sin(60^\circ-x)}=\frac{-\sin 2x}{\sin^2 60^\circ-\sin^2 x}=\frac{-\sin 2x}{\frac{3-4\sin^2 x}{4}}=\frac{-8\sin x\cos x}{3-4\sin^2 x}.\]

Add \(\cot x\):

\[f(x)=\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}-\frac{8\sin x\cos x}{3-4\sin^2 x}=\frac{\cos x\,(3-4\sin^2 x)-8\sin^2 x\cos x}{\sin x\,(3-4\sin^2 x)}=\frac{3\cos x\,(1-4\sin^2 x)}{3\sin x-4\sin^3 x}.\]

The denominator is \(\sin 3x\), and \(\cos 3x=\cos x\,(4\cos^2 x-3)=\cos x\,(1-4\sin^2 x)\), so the numerator is \(3\cos 3x\).

\[f(x)=\frac{3\cos 3x}{\sin 3x}=3\cot 3x.\]

\[=\tan 60^\circ=\sqrt3.\]

\[\tan\theta+\cot\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}=\frac{\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}=\frac{2}{\sin 2\theta}.\]

Here \(\theta=\dfrac{3\pi}{16}\), so \(2\theta=\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\) and \(\sin\dfrac{3\pi}{8}=\cos\dfrac{\pi}{8}=\sqrt{\dfrac{1+\cos\frac{\pi}{4}}{2}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{1+\frac{1}{\sqrt2}}{2}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{2+\sqrt2}}{2}.\)

\[\tan\frac{3\pi}{16}+\cot\frac{3\pi}{16}=\frac{2}{\sin\frac{3\pi}{8}}=\frac{4}{\sqrt{2+\sqrt2}}=\frac{4\sqrt{2-\sqrt2}}{\sqrt{(2+\sqrt2)(2-\sqrt2)}}=\frac{4\sqrt{2-\sqrt2}}{\sqrt2}=2\sqrt2\,\sqrt{2-\sqrt2}=2\sqrt{4-2\sqrt2}\approx 2.165.\]

Note: The exact value is \(2\sqrt2\sqrt{2-\sqrt2}=2\sqrt{4-2\sqrt2}\approx2.165\). As printed, option C \(=2\sqrt{2-\sqrt2}\approx1.53\), which is not equal to it (and A and D are printed identically). Option C is the one the key intends — it is missing a factor of \(\sqrt2\) — so mark C, but remember the true value.

questions.questionText: If \(\theta\) is an acute angle and \(\sin\dfrac{\theta}{2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{x-1}{2x}}\), then \(\tan\theta\) is equal to
questions.explanation:
\[\cos^2\frac\theta2=1-\frac{x-1}{2x}=\frac{x+1}{2x}\;\Rightarrow\;\cos\frac\theta2=\sqrt{\frac{x+1}{2x}},\qquad \tan\frac\theta2=\sqrt{\frac{x-1}{x+1}}.\]

Now \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{2\tan\frac\theta2}{1-\tan^2\frac\theta2}\):

\[\tan\theta=\frac{2\sqrt{\frac{x-1}{x+1}}}{1-\frac{x-1}{x+1}}=\frac{2\sqrt{\frac{x-1}{x+1}}}{\frac{2}{x+1}}=(x+1)\sqrt{\frac{x-1}{x+1}}=\sqrt{(x+1)(x-1)}=\sqrt{x^2-1}.\]

\[E=\frac{1-\cos 92^\circ}{\sin 92^\circ}=\frac{2\sin^2 46^\circ}{2\sin 46^\circ\cos 46^\circ}=\tan 46^\circ=\cot 44^\circ.\]

Put \(\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{2^{10}}\). Then \(\dfrac{\pi}{2^{9}}=2\theta,\;\dfrac{\pi}{2^{8}}=4\theta,\ldots,\dfrac{\pi}{2^{2}}=2^{8}\theta\), so the product is

\[\sin\theta\cos\theta\cos 2\theta\cos 4\theta\cdots\cos 2^{8}\theta\]

— nine cosines. Using \(\cos\theta\cos2\theta\cdots\cos2^{n-1}\theta=\dfrac{\sin 2^n\theta}{2^n\sin\theta}\) with \(n=9\):

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If \(\theta=3\alpha\) and \(\sin\theta=\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}\), then the value of the expression \(a\csc\alpha-b\sec\alpha\) is:
questions.explanation:
\(\sin 3\alpha=\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}\) gives \(\cos 3\alpha=\dfrac{b}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}\) (taking the positive root). So \(a=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\,\sin3\alpha\) and \(b=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\,\cos 3\alpha\).

\[a\csc\alpha-b\sec\alpha=\frac{a\cos\alpha-b\sin\alpha}{\sin\alpha\cos\alpha}=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\cdot\frac{\sin3\alpha\cos\alpha-\cos3\alpha\sin\alpha}{\sin\alpha\cos\alpha}=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\cdot\frac{\sin 2\alpha}{\sin\alpha\cos\alpha}=2\sqrt{a^2+b^2}.\]

questions.explanation:

questions.questionText: If \(\dfrac{\sec 8\theta-1}{\sec 4\theta-1}=\dfrac{a+b\tan^2 2\theta}{1+c\tan^2 2\theta+d\tan^4 2\theta}\) (where \(\theta\neq\dfrac{n\pi}{16},\ n\in I\)), then the value of \((a-b+c-d)\) is
questions.explanation:
First, \(\dfrac{\sec 8\theta-1}{\sec 4\theta-1}=\tan 8\theta\cot 2\theta\) (proved in Q15). Now put \(t=\tan 2\theta\):

\[\tan 4\theta=\frac{2t}{1-t^2},\qquad \tan 8\theta=\frac{2\tan4\theta}{1-\tan^24\theta}=\frac{\frac{4t}{1-t^2}}{1-\frac{4t^2}{(1-t^2)^2}}=\frac{4t(1-t^2)}{(1-t^2)^2-4t^2}=\frac{4t(1-t^2)}{1-6t^2+t^4}.\]

\[\tan 8\theta\cot 2\theta=\frac{4(1-t^2)}{1-6t^2+t^4}=\frac{4-4\tan^2 2\theta}{1-6\tan^2 2\theta+\tan^4 2\theta}.\]

Comparing: \(a=4,\ b=-4,\ c=-6,\ d=1\).

\[a-b+c-d=4+4-6-1=1.\]

Let the common value be \(\lambda\neq0\). Then \(\dfrac1x=\dfrac{\cos\theta}{\lambda},\ \dfrac1y=\dfrac{\cos(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3})}{\lambda},\ \dfrac1z=\dfrac{\cos(\theta+\frac{4\pi}{3})}{\lambda}\), so

\[\frac1x+\frac1y+\frac1z=\frac1\lambda\left[\cos\theta+\cos\!\left(\theta+\tfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)+\cos\!\left(\theta+\tfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)\right].\]

First and third terms: \(\cos\theta+\cos\left(\theta+\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)=2\cos\left(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}=-\cos\left(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\). The bracket is therefore \(0\), and the sum is \(0\).

Key identity: \(\cot\theta-\tan\theta=\dfrac{\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}=\dfrac{\cos 2\theta}{\frac12\sin 2\theta}=2\cot 2\theta\), i.e. \(\tan\theta+2\cot 2\theta=\cot\theta\). Telescope from the right:

\[4\tan 4\alpha+8\cot 8\alpha=4(\tan 4\alpha+2\cot 8\alpha)=4\cot 4\alpha\]

\[2\tan 2\alpha+4\cot 4\alpha=2(\tan 2\alpha+2\cot 4\alpha)=2\cot 2\alpha\]

\[\tan\alpha+2\cot 2\alpha=\cot\alpha.\]

Note \(\cos\frac{3\pi}{7}=-\cos\frac{4\pi}{7}\), so \(P=-\cos\frac{\pi}{7}\cos\frac{2\pi}{7}\cos\frac{4\pi}{7}\). Multiply and divide by \(2\sin\frac{\pi}{7}\) and use \(2\sin\theta\cos\theta=\sin 2\theta\) repeatedly:

\[\cos\frac{\pi}{7}\cos\frac{2\pi}{7}\cos\frac{4\pi}{7}=\frac{2\sin\frac{\pi}{7}\cos\frac{\pi}{7}\cos\frac{2\pi}{7}\cos\frac{4\pi}{7}}{2\sin\frac{\pi}{7}}=\frac{\sin\frac{2\pi}{7}\cos\frac{2\pi}{7}\cos\frac{4\pi}{7}}{2\sin\frac{\pi}{7}}=\frac{\sin\frac{4\pi}{7}\cos\frac{4\pi}{7}}{4\sin\frac{\pi}{7}}=\frac{\sin\frac{8\pi}{7}}{8\sin\frac{\pi}{7}}.\]

Since \(\sin\frac{8\pi}{7}=\sin\left(\pi+\frac{\pi}{7}\right)=-\sin\frac{\pi}{7}\), this equals \(-\dfrac18\), and therefore

\[P=\cos\frac{\pi}{7}\cos\frac{2\pi}{7}\cos\frac{3\pi}{7}=\frac18.\]

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If \(A,B,C,D\) are the angles of a cyclic quadrilateral taken in order, then \(\cos(180^\circ+A)+\cos(180^\circ-B)+\cos(180^\circ-C)-\sin(90^\circ-D)=\)
questions.explanation:
In a cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles are supplementary: \(A+C=180^\circ,\ B+D=180^\circ\).

\[\cos(180^\circ+A)=-\cos A,\quad\cos(180^\circ-B)=-\cos B,\quad\cos(180^\circ-C)=-\cos C,\quad\sin(90^\circ-D)=\cos D.\]

\[\text{Expression}=-(\cos A+\cos C)-(\cos B+\cos D).\]

\(\cos C=\cos(180^\circ-A)=-\cos A\) and \(\cos D=-\cos B\), so both brackets vanish and the value is \(0\).

Reduce each piece:

\[\tan\!\left(x-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=-\cot x,\quad \cos\!\left(\tfrac{3\pi}{2}+x\right)=\sin x,\quad \sin\!\left(\tfrac{7\pi}{2}-x\right)=\sin\!\left(\tfrac{3\pi}{2}-x\right)=-\cos x,\]

\[\cos\!\left(x-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=\sin x,\quad \tan\!\left(\tfrac{3\pi}{2}+x\right)=-\cot x.\]

\[\frac{(-\cot x)(\sin x)-(-\cos x)^3}{(\sin x)(-\cot x)}=\frac{-\cos x+\cos^3 x}{-\cos x}=\frac{-\cos x\,(1-\cos^2 x)}{-\cos x}=1-\cos^2x=\sin^2 x.\]

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If \(\csc\theta=\dfrac{p+q}{p-q}\) \((p\neq q\neq0)\), then \(\left|\cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}+\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)\right|\) is equal to
questions.explanation:
\(\sin\theta=\dfrac{p-q}{p+q}\). Now

\[\cot\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\theta}{2}\right)=\frac{1-\tan\frac\theta2}{1+\tan\frac\theta2}=\frac{\cos\frac\theta2-\sin\frac\theta2}{\cos\frac\theta2+\sin\frac\theta2}.\]

Square it:

\[\cot^2\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\theta}{2}\right)=\frac{1-2\sin\frac\theta2\cos\frac\theta2}{1+2\sin\frac\theta2\cos\frac\theta2}=\frac{1-\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta}=\frac{1-\frac{p-q}{p+q}}{1+\frac{p-q}{p+q}}=\frac{2q}{2p}=\frac qp.\]

\[\therefore\;\left|\cot\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\theta}{2}\right)\right|=\sqrt{\frac qp}.\]

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If \(\sin t+\cos t=\dfrac15\), then \(\tan\dfrac t2\) is equal to:
questions.explanation:
Let \(y=\tan\dfrac t2\). Then \(\sin t=\dfrac{2y}{1+y^2},\ \cos t=\dfrac{1-y^2}{1+y^2}\):

\[\frac{2y+1-y^2}{1+y^2}=\frac15\;\Rightarrow\;10y+5-5y^2=1+y^2\;\Rightarrow\;6y^2-10y-4=0\;\Rightarrow\;3y^2-5y-2=0.\]

\[(3y+1)(y-2)=0\;\Rightarrow\;y=2\ \text{ or }\ y=-\tfrac13.\]

Check: \(y=2\) gives \(\sin t=\frac45,\cos t=-\frac35\); \(y=-\frac13\) gives \(\sin t=-\frac35,\cos t=\frac45\). Both sum to \(\frac15\), so both are valid.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If the value of \(\dfrac{3\cos 36^\circ+5\sin 18^\circ}{5\cos 36^\circ-3\sin 18^\circ}\) is \(\dfrac{a\sqrt5-b}{c}\), where \(a,b,c\) are natural numbers and \(\gcd(a,c)=1\), then \(a+b+c\) is equal to:
questions.explanation:
\(\cos 36^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt5+1}{4}\), \(\sin 18^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{4}\). Multiplying numerator and denominator by 4:

\[\frac{3(\sqrt5+1)+5(\sqrt5-1)}{5(\sqrt5+1)-3(\sqrt5-1)}=\frac{8\sqrt5-2}{2\sqrt5+8}=\frac{4\sqrt5-1}{\sqrt5+4}.\]

Rationalise with \(4-\sqrt5\):

\[\frac{(4\sqrt5-1)(4-\sqrt5)}{16-5}=\frac{16\sqrt5-20-4+\sqrt5}{11}=\frac{17\sqrt5-24}{11}.\]

\(a=17,\ b=24,\ c=11\) (and \(\gcd(17,11)=1\)), so \(a+b+c=52\).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If \(\sin\alpha=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt5}\) and \(\sin\beta=\dfrac35\), then \(\beta-\alpha\) lies in the interval
questions.explanation:
Taking \(\alpha,\beta\) acute: \(\cos\alpha=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt5}\), \(\cos\beta=\dfrac45\).

\[\sin(\beta-\alpha)=\sin\beta\cos\alpha-\cos\beta\sin\alpha=\frac35\cdot\frac2{\sqrt5}-\frac45\cdot\frac1{\sqrt5}=\frac{2}{5\sqrt5}\approx0.179>0,\]

\[\cos(\beta-\alpha)=\cos\beta\cos\alpha+\sin\beta\sin\alpha=\frac{8}{5\sqrt5}+\frac{3}{5\sqrt5}=\frac{11}{5\sqrt5}>0.\]

So \(\beta-\alpha\) is in the first quadrant with \(\sin(\beta-\alpha)<\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\approx0.707\), giving \(0<\beta-\alpha<\dfrac{\pi}{4}\).

questions.explanation:

\[\tan 2\alpha=\tan[(\alpha+\beta)+(\alpha-\beta)]=\frac{\frac34+\frac5{12}}{1-\frac34\cdot\frac5{12}}=\frac{\frac{14}{12}}{\frac{33}{48}}=\frac{14}{12}\cdot\frac{48}{33}=\frac{56}{33}.\]

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If \(\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{18}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{18}\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{18}\right)=K\), then the value of \(\sin\left(\dfrac{10K\pi}{3}\right)\) is:
questions.explanation:
In degrees: \(K=\sin 10^\circ\sin 50^\circ\sin 70^\circ=\sin\theta\,\sin(60^\circ-\theta)\,\sin(60^\circ+\theta)\) with \(\theta=10^\circ\), and this product equals \(\dfrac14\sin 3\theta\):

\[K=\frac14\sin 30^\circ=\frac18.\]

\[\sin\!\left(\frac{10K\pi}{3}\right)=\sin\!\left(\frac{10\pi}{24}\right)=\sin\frac{5\pi}{12}=\sin 75^\circ=\sin 45^\circ\cos 30^\circ+\cos 45^\circ\sin 30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3+1}{2\sqrt2}.\]

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: Let \(\cos(\alpha+\beta)=-\dfrac{1}{10}\) and \(\sin(\alpha-\beta)=\dfrac38\), where \(0<\alpha<\dfrac{\pi}{3}\) and \(0<\beta<\dfrac{\pi}{4}\). If \(\tan 2\alpha=\dfrac{3(1-r\sqrt5)}{\sqrt{11}(s+\sqrt5)}\), where \(r,s\in\mathbb N\), then \(r+s\) is equal to
questions.explanation:
\(0<\alpha+\beta<\frac{7\pi}{12}\) and \(\cos(\alpha+\beta)<0\), so \(\frac{\pi}{2}<\alpha+\beta<\frac{7\pi}{12}\): sine positive.

\[\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\sqrt{1-\tfrac{1}{100}}=\frac{3\sqrt{11}}{10},\qquad \tan(\alpha+\beta)=\frac{3\sqrt{11}/10}{-1/10}=-3\sqrt{11}.\]

\(-\frac{\pi}{4}0\), so cosine positive:

\[\cos(\alpha-\beta)=\sqrt{1-\tfrac{9}{64}}=\frac{\sqrt{55}}{8},\qquad \tan(\alpha-\beta)=\frac{3}{\sqrt{55}}.\]

\[\tan 2\alpha=\frac{\tan(\alpha+\beta)+\tan(\alpha-\beta)}{1-\tan(\alpha+\beta)\tan(\alpha-\beta)}=\frac{-3\sqrt{11}+\frac{3}{\sqrt{55}}}{1+\frac{9\sqrt{11}}{\sqrt{55}}}.\]

Multiply top and bottom by \(\sqrt{55}\), using \(\sqrt{11}\sqrt{55}=\sqrt{605}=11\sqrt5\):

\[\tan 2\alpha=\frac{-33\sqrt5+3}{\sqrt{55}+9\sqrt{11}}=\frac{3(1-11\sqrt5)}{\sqrt{11}(\sqrt5+9)}.\]

So \(r=11,\ s=9\) and \(r+s=20\).

\(\dfrac{7\pi}{9}=\dfrac{4\pi}{9}+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\). Let \(\phi=x+\dfrac{4\pi}{9}\); since \(\dfrac{\pi}{9}<x<\dfrac{\pi}{3}\), we get \(\dfrac{5\pi}{9}<\phi<\dfrac{7\pi}{9}\) (second quadrant), so \(\cos\phi=-\sqrt{1-a^2}\).

\[\cos\!\left(\phi+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\cos\phi\cos\frac{\pi}{3}-\sin\phi\sin\frac{\pi}{3}=-\sqrt{1-a^2}\cdot\frac12-a\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}=\frac{-\sqrt{1-a^2}-a\sqrt3}{2}.\]

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If \(\sin x-\sin y=\dfrac12\) and \(\cos x-\cos y=1\), then \(\tan(x+y)\) is equal to
questions.explanation:
\[\sin x-\sin y=2\cos\frac{x+y}{2}\sin\frac{x-y}{2}=\frac12,\qquad \cos x-\cos y=-2\sin\frac{x+y}{2}\sin\frac{x-y}{2}=1.\]

Divide the second by the first:

\[-\tan\frac{x+y}{2}=2\;\Rightarrow\;\tan\frac{x+y}{2}=-2.\]

\[\tan(x+y)=\frac{2\tan\frac{x+y}{2}}{1-\tan^2\frac{x+y}{2}}=\frac{2(-2)}{1-4}=\frac{-4}{-3}=\frac43.\]

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If \(\sin^3 x\,\sin 3x=\displaystyle\sum_{m=0}^{n}c_m\cos mx\), where \(c_0,c_1,\ldots,c_n\) are constants and \(c_n\neq0\), then the value of \(n\) is

From \(\sin 3x=3\sin x-4\sin^3x\): \(\sin^3x=\dfrac{3\sin x-\sin 3x}{4}\).

questions.questionText: If \(\dfrac{\tan 3A}{\tan A}=a\), then \(\dfrac{\sin 3A}{\sin A}\) is equal to
questions.explanation:
\[\frac{\tan 3A}{\tan A}=\frac{3-\tan^2A}{1-3\tan^2A}=a\;\Rightarrow\;3-\tan^2A=a-3a\tan^2A\;\Rightarrow\;\tan^2A=\frac{a-3}{3a-1}.\]

\[\sin^2A=\frac{\tan^2A}{1+\tan^2A}=\frac{a-3}{(3a-1)+(a-3)}=\frac{a-3}{4(a-1)}.\]

\[\frac{\sin 3A}{\sin A}=3-4\sin^2A=3-\frac{a-3}{a-1}=\frac{3a-3-a+3}{a-1}=\frac{2a}{a-1}.\]

Divide by \(\cos\alpha\cos\beta\ (\neq0)\): \(\tan\alpha=-5\tan\beta\), so \(k=-5\).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: If \(\tan\theta+\tan\left(\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)+\tan\left(\theta+\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)=3\), then which of the following is equal to \(1\)?
questions.explanation:
Let \(t=\tan\theta\). Then \(\tan\left(\theta+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\dfrac{t+\sqrt3}{1-\sqrt3t}\) and \(\tan\left(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)=\dfrac{t-\sqrt3}{1+\sqrt3t}\).

\[\frac{t+\sqrt3}{1-\sqrt3t}+\frac{t-\sqrt3}{1+\sqrt3t}=\frac{(t+\sqrt3)(1+\sqrt3t)+(t-\sqrt3)(1-\sqrt3t)}{1-3t^2}=\frac{8t}{1-3t^2}.\]

\[t+\frac{8t}{1-3t^2}=\frac{9t-3t^3}{1-3t^2}=3\cdot\frac{3t-t^3}{1-3t^2}=3\tan 3\theta.\]

So \(3\tan 3\theta=3\Rightarrow\tan 3\theta=1\).
